scope: Align selected-applet SELECT status, CLA/chaining admission, NDEF INS-only dispatch/finalization and FIDO terminal INS validation with C3.1.2.
mapping: The exact global SELECT discriminator is CLA00/INS A4/P1=04. Noncanonical SELECT reaches the selected applet. C Admin/PIV/OpenPGP check P1/P2 after CLA; Rust now returns6A86 for their local SELECT instead of unsupported INS.

OpenPGP strips CLA chain bit only for certificate PUT DATA, key IMPORT and PSO decipher, matching the C handler. The host OpenPGP helper sends ordinary objects including Lc255 URL in one short APDU; its certificate fragmentation remains193 bytes. One initial full CTest exposed this fixture policy mismatch; the corrected fixture is independently checked by E66 URL schedules.

C NDEF has no CLA filter. Rust now accepts any CLA, adjusts SELECT/READ chain headers to final, and keeps only the UPDATE chain bit with canonicalized continuation offsets. Engine uses that same adjusted header for end_frame, not the original CLA bit.

C FIDO rejects CLA10. Proprietary intermediate CLA90 fragments acknowledge before INS dispatch; Rust defers unsupported INS until terminal finish and rejects before CBOR dispatch. The terminal header is supplied through the existing registry finish call, with no new request storage.

The deterministic main612-case generator derives expected outputs from dispatch rules. Six additional URL/NDEF schedules check rejected chained URL, valid short Lc255 URL, retained grants/response prefixes and contiguous NDEF writes using arbitrary CLA. No implementation outputs are copied into expectations.
